plan: In a private-values, second-price auction with rational opponents and independent uniform values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Overbidding risks negative profit if the second-highest bid exceeds your value; underbidding risks losing positive-profit wins. There is only one round, so no dynamic signaling. With value 25, bidding 25 maximizes expected profit: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid and earn at least 0; if I lose, I earn 0.

[ Second-price auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding is (weakly) dominant: bidding my value maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds my value, yielding negative surplus; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With value = 3 and no history (1 round), there’s no learning adjustment. Others are rational and likely to bid their values, so matching my value is optimal. I will bid exactly $3.0 in $0.1 increments. ]

[ This is a second‑price sealed‑bid auction (Vickrey). With independent private values and rational opponents, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks negative profit if you win and pay above your value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. There’s only 1 round, so no learning or signaling value. Therefore, bid exactly $26.0. ]
